ev.q: Multivariable logit models were used to estimate adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) between BMI categories and four outcomes of interest
Approximately 1.8% of patients had underweight, 28.3% had overweight, and 50.8% had obesity
Among 71,491 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 (48.1% of all COVID-19 patients), 34,896 (48.8%) required ICU admission
Approximately 1.8% of patients had underweight, 28.3% had overweight, and 50.8% had obesity
Patients with COVID-19 with underweight had a 20% (95% CI = 16%–25%) higher risk for hospitalization than did those with a healthy weight
Analyses were then stratified by age (<65 years versus ≥65 years)
Associations with risk for hospitalization and death were pronounced among adults aged <65 years
Data for this study were obtained from PHD-SR, a large, hospital-based, all-payer database

methods_quotes.q: Multivariable logit models were used to estimate adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) between BMI categories and four outcomes of interest
Models used robust standard errors clustered on hospital identification
modeled as fractional polynomials to account for nonlinear associations
Analyses were then stratified by age (<65 years versus ≥65 years)
A second sensitivity analysis used multiple imputation for missing BMIs
Risks were reestimated for different age categories, after including interactions between age category and BMI
